newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Croats block refugee returns -- UN.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Croats block refugee returns -- UN.

text.p: U.N. relief officials said on Friday that Bosnian Croat authorities had prevented Moslem refugees from returning to their homes and blocked free movement of people in a series of incidents over the past week.

Mans Nyberg, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), said the incidents showed a "hardening attitude on the part of the Croat authorities in the (Moslem- Croat) federation regarding freedom of movement and minority returns."
Last Sunday, Croat officials in the western town of Drvar prevented the return of 250 displaced Serbs who made the journey from Serb-held territory, Nyberg said.
The group was turned back by demonstrators incited by local authorities in a "typical rent-a-crowd scenario", he said.
A Moslem family was evicted from their home in the Croat sector of Mostar on Wednesday, bringing the number of evictions to 54 so far this year in the divided community.

A crowd of Croat women blocked and stoned a bus bringing Moslems from a visit to Croat-held Capljina in the west on Thursday. The crowd dispersed only after a nearby NATO patrol fired several shots in the air, Nyberg told reporters.

In the southern town of Stolac, the Croat mayor sent a letter to the UNHCR on Thursday informing them of his inability to provide security for a planned visit of former Moslem residents who wanted to see their homes this weekend.
"This list of events is of great concern, especially since they have been occurring during a short period of time," he said.
Moslems and Croats fought a war in 1993 as a side-show to the main conflict with Bosnian Serb forces, which ended in a U.S.-brokered accord in March 1994.
The Moslem and Croats agreed to form a federation and the accord stopped the fighting, but rival authorities dragged their feet when it came to allowing the return of minorities.
Both sides resist power-sharing agreements where they form a majority and Croat nationalist leaders remain committed to creating a separate state linked to neighbouring Croatia.
Meanwhile, Serb authorities continue to discourage the resettlement of Moslem refugees in Serb-controlled territory.
